title: Model profile stewardship: rolling attestations, sampled regression detectors, and pin-safe migrations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and ship an operational playbook and lightweight automation for publishing and maintaining Redwood-verified performance profiles that minimizes user disruption during profile refreshes and model version migrations. This ticket covers three interlocking capabilities: (1) rolling attestation signatures derived from sampled production shadowing and deterministic synthetic probes, (2) sampled regression detectors that continuously monitor latency, throughput, and cost deltas against anchors and trigger re-verification, and (3) pin-safe migration patterns (staggered pin, fallback pin, and cost-normalized rollouts) plus the Console UX and telemetry contracts to support them.

Scope details:
- Attestation flow: capture a compact attestation bundle (fingerprint, sample traces, metric buckets, cost-normalized baselines) signed by the perf-signing service when a profile is published. Attestations are time-windowed (rolling 7-day window) to make profiles reflect recent workload shapes while avoiding thrash.
- Sampled production shadowing: lightweight, token-limited shadow requests sampled at <0.5% of live traffic for candidate profiles with strict rate limits and privacy filters (strip PII). Shadow telemetry is aggregated into summary histograms for quick comparison rather than storing raw traces.
- Regression detectors: streaming jobs that compute statistically-significant deltas (p90 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-k) against pinned anchors. Configurable thresholds by tier (hosted/dedicated/private) and region. On detection the detector will open a reverify workflow instead of automatically rolling back.
- Pin-safe migrations: define a migration contract: canary fleet at 1% traffic for 24h, stagger to 10%/50%/100% with automated health gating, fallback pin available within 2min of failure, and explicit console approval for >50% changes. Include cost-normalization across regions to prevent false positives from regional price skews.
- Console/UX: add a publish checklist (attestation status, shadow sample count, cost delta estimate), a pin migration wizard, and a compact history view of attestations and reverify outcomes.
- Telemetry/observability: add per-profile verification metrics, attestation hash, sample counts, and a health signal that feeds the existing profile catalog dashboard and SLO alerts.

Non-goals: automatic unreviewed profile republishing, storing raw request payloads for shadowing, or changes to model training/onboarding pipelines.

Success criteria:
- New publish flow emits an attestation bundle 95% of the time for candidate profiles in staging.
- Regression detector false-positive rate <3% on historical replay.
- Console shows migration wizard and can complete a staggered pin migration with one confirmed rollback path.

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We chose sampled shadowing with summarized telemetry vs full request capture to balance privacy and signal.
- Attestation windows are set to 7 days to balance recency and stability; this can be parameterized per-model class later.
- Initial thresholds will be conservative P1/P2 style; tuning will happen during the rollout cycle.

Open questions:
- Should attestations be cryptographically signed with customer SCM for Private deployments? (security asked for a follow-up).
- How aggressive should the cost-normalization smoothing be to avoid gating benign currency or region-level price changes?

updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created during PM/Eng sync. Scoped initial MVP and aligned on privacy constraints for shadow sampling.
2026-02-25: Eng spike completed. Prototype attestation writer exists in branch 'perf/attest-bundle' and emits compact JSON hashes. PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/12345.
2026-03-02: Design reviewed Console migration wizard. Feedback to reduce copy and emphasize rollback affordances. Updated mocks in Drive.
2026-03-05: Reliability reviewed detector thresholds; recommended staged rollout with historical replay against last 90 days of traffic to calibrate false-positive rates.
2026-03-10: PM acceptance criteria refined and added release gating: must pass shadow-sample coverage >= 2000 requests in staging and detector false-positive <3% on replay.
Next steps: finalize telemetry contract (ENG to provide metric names), implement canary gating in routing layer, and implement attestation signing for Private deployments as a follow-up ticket.
comments: Marcus Li (ENG): Found that summarizing latency into logarithmic buckets reduces storage by ~8x while preserving signal for p90/p95 comparisons.
Priya Nayar (Security): OK with summarized shadowing if PII removal is enforced at the agent; follow-up required for Private/KMS signing.
Ben Cho (Design): Need an explicit 'emergency rollback' CTA in the migration wizard that documents what will happen to in-flight traffic.
QA note: create a synthetic replay harness for common customer workloads and add tests for canary gating behavior.
Link to related work: PM-61420 (embed-cost-estimates-into-verified-profiles) provides the cost normalization helpers we will reuse.
